1.explanation: The file src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js exports three key arrays: KEYWORDS, LITERALS, and TYPES, and then combines them into BUILT_INS. The TYPE array is what drives highlighting of global built-in types (e.g. Number, String, Date, etc.). BigInt (and the BigInt-typed arrays) are missing from this TYPES list, so the highlighter never treats them as built-in types. Adding “BigInt”, “BigInt64Array” and “BigUint64Array” to the TYPES array (and thus to BUILT_INS) will enable correct highlighting.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting JavaScript code, the built-in BigInt type (and its related typed array forms) is not being treated as a type. The screenshots show that “BigInt” is tokenized as an ordinary identifier (or string literal) instead of being highlighted the same way “Number” and other built-ins are. The expected behavior is that BigInt, BigInt64Array, and BigUint64Array appear in the same “builtin type” color as other global objects.

2.explanation: The bug stems from the constant TYPES in src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js, which defines the list of built-in global types that highlight.js will classify as types. BigInt, BigInt64Array and BigUint64Array are missing from this array, so they are never promoted to the “built_in” type category. By adding these entries to the TYPES list, highlight.js will recognize and highlight them correctly.
